What it does

This law requires healthcare providers and healthcare facilities that use artificial intelligence to document in person or telehealth visits to notify patients of that use. It also requires those providers and facilities to review the documentation generated by AI for accuracy after the visit. The purpose is to ensure patients are properly notified of AI use by healthcare providers.

Who it applies to

  • Healthcare providers and healthcare facilities that employ artificial intelligence to document in person or telehealth visits (Sec. 23-106-3).

Effective date

upon passage

Key definitions

  • Artificial Intelligence or AI: any technology that can simulate human intelligence including, but not limited to, natural language processing, training language models, reinforcement learning from human feedback and machine learning systems (Sec. 23-106-2(1)).
  • Healthcare facility: shall have the same meaning as § 23-17-2 (Sec. 23-106-2(2)).
  • Healthcare provider: physicians, physician assistants, dentists, registered nurses, licensed practical nurses, advanced practice registered nurses, nursing assistants, or any other healthcare professional licensed by the director of the department of health (Sec. 23-106-2(3)).

Obligations

  • Notify patients of the use of AI to document in person or telehealth visits (Sec. 23-106-3).
  • Review the documentation generated by AI for accuracy after the visit (Sec. 23-106-3).

Prohibitions

  • not stated in the text

Penalties and enforcement

not stated in the text

How it affects AI deployment

  • Organizations using AI to document in person or telehealth visits must notify patients of that use (Sec. 23-106-3).
  • Organizations must review the documentation generated by AI for accuracy after each visit (Sec. 23-106-3).
  • The requirement applies to both in person and telehealth visits (Sec. 23-106-3).

Notable exemptions

  • not stated in the text

Compliance steps

  • Determine whether the organization is a healthcare provider or healthcare facility under the definitions (Sec. 23-106-2(2), (3)).
  • Identify any use of AI to document in person or telehealth visits (Sec. 23-106-3).
  • Notify patients of the use of AI for that sole purpose (Sec. 23-106-3).
  • Review the documentation generated by AI for accuracy after the visit (Sec. 23-106-3).

 STATE OF RHODE ISLAND

 IN GENERAL ASSEMBLY

 JANUARY SESSION, A.D. 2026
 ____________


 AN ACT

 RELATING TO HEALTH AND SAFETY -- USE OF ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE BY
 HEALTHCARE PROVIDERS NOTIFICATION ACT



 Introduced By: Senators Lauria, Valverde, Murray, DiMario, Mack, Euer, Urso,
 Kallman, Thompson, and Gu
 Date Introduced: February 13, 2026

 Referred To: Senate Health & Human Services




 It is enacted by the General Assembly as follows:

 1 SECTION 1. Title 23 of the General Laws entitled "HEALTH AND SAFETY" is hereby

 2 amended by adding thereto the following chapter:

 3 CHAPTER 106

 4 USE OF ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE BY HEALTHCARE PROVIDERS NOTIFICATION

 5 ACT

 6 23-106-1. Short title and purpose.

 7 (a) This chapter shall be known and may be cited as the "Use of Artificial Intelligence by

 8 Healthcare Providers Notification Act".

 9 (b) The purpose of this chapter is to ensure patients are properly notified of the use of

10 artificial intelligence by healthcare providers.

11 23-106-2. Definitions.

12 As used in this chapter, the following terms shall have the following meanings:

13 (1) "Artificial Intelligence" or "AI" means any technology that can simulate human

14 intelligence including, but not limited to, natural language processing, training language models,

15 reinforcement learning from human feedback and machine learning systems.

16 (2) "Healthcare facility" shall have the same meaning as § 23-17-2.

17 (3) "Healthcare provider" means physicians, physician assistants, dentists, registered

18 nurses, licensed practical nurses, advanced practice registered nurses, nursing assistants, or any
 1 other healthcare professional licensed by the director of the department of health.

2 23-106-3. Notifications required.

3 Any and all healthcare providers and healthcare facilities that employ artificial intelligence

4 ("AI") to document in-person or telehealth visits shall notify patients of the use of AI for that sole

5 purpose and review the AI-generated documentation for accuracy after the visit.

6 SECTION 2. This act shall take effect upon passage.
